full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: This appeal by leave by the defendants is from the judgment and order of a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division dated 25.11.91 in Civil Revision No. 4012 of 1991 (Dhaka)/Civil Revision No. 58 of 1988 (Jessore) discharging the Rule and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 15.9.87 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. Narail in Title Appeal No. 29 of 1985 dismissing the same and affirming those dated 31.12.85 passed by the learned Munsif, Narail in Title Suit No. 386 of 1979, decreeing the suit. 

 4. The trial Court disbelieved the case of illness of the plaintiff and found that the plaintiff had some laches in forwarding successive medical certificates without subjecting himself to a medical examination by his employer and the defendants too had laches as they never directed the plaintiff to face a Medical Board. The trial Court also found beyond any reasonable doubt that the plaintiff was actually carrying on some business at the time of his so-called illness. His recorded address in the department was village Sowal Bathan. Post Office Bagarsram, District Jessore but he did not send any information to his department on any change of address. The trial Court found that the impugned letter of discharge was sent to the recorded address of the plaintiff but the defendant knew his latest Magura address but did not care to send the letter of discharge to his known Magura address or to cause the letter of discharge to be published in the press. The trial Court found that the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules 1976 were not complied with. It therefore decreed the suit. 

 5. The appellate Court below held that it was unnecessary to consider whether the plaintiffs’ absence was authorized or not. A show cause notice ought to have been sent to the Magura address of the plaintiff or at least it could have been published in a newspaper. The plaintiff was not given any opportunity to defend himself under the 1976 Rules. Further, there is no such punishment called "discharge" in the said Rules. The appellate Court below found from a letter of appointment filed by the plaintiff in the appellate Court that he was appointed by the Chief Engineer. Therefore the order of discharge passed by the Superintending Engineer, Khulna Division was without jurisdiction. The lower appellate Court therefore affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court 

 7. Leave was granted to consider the Government-appellant's contention that the plaintiff having failed to prove that his appointing authority was the Chief Engineer and the Superintending Engineer being the appointing authority of Lower Division Assistants, the High Court Division erred in law in affirming the judgment of the lower appellate Court. The show cause notice having been sent to the unchanged recorded address of the plaintiff there was no requirement of sending the same to his Magura address or for publishing the same in any newspaper. The High Court Division was wrong in not giving its decision on the issue of service of show cause notice. As the plaintiff on the finding of the trial Court was indulging in business at the time of his so-called illness and the lower appellate Court having erroneously held that it was unnecessary to consider whether the plaintiffs’ absence was authorized or not, the High Court Division acted illegally in upholding the decree upon overlooking the same.
